newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch ban transport of pigs in south of country.
newsitem.headline: Dutch ban transport of pigs in south of country.

text.p: The Dutch government, battling to control a swine fever epidemic, has banned the transport of pigs over about a third of the country.
The outbreak now affects some 95 farms in the south of the Netherlands, and around 800,000 pigs have been destroyed.

"The transport of pigs is not possible in the area south of the river Waal (excluding Zeeland)," a Farm Ministry spokesman told Reuters. "We hope these new measures will contain the disease but we fear there will be more cases."

Last week the government put some 1,600 farms across the country on its "high inspection" list because they had received pig sperm from the original infected area. The slightest sign of swine fever at any of these farms would lead to all pigs there being killed.
Since the outbreak, many of the country's trading partners, including the U.S. have banned imports of Dutch pigs and pork products.
Last year the Netherlands -- which has some 14 million pigs - exported almost a million tonnes of pigs and pork products, bringing in around 5.1 billion guilders.
